question: Who among the following was the first and longest serving Attorney General of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Motilal Chimanlal Sitalwad**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motilal Chimanlal Sitalwad** was the first and longest serving Attorney General of India.
 
• He served as the Attorney General from **28 January 1950 to 1 March 1963**.
 
• Sitalwad played a significant role in shaping the legal system of newly independent India.
 
• His tenure is noted for laying down the foundation for the Attorney General's office and its operations in India.
 
• He was succeeded by C.K. Daphtary after his tenure ended.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Attorney General of India** is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President of India under Article 76(1) of the Constitution and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Attorney General has the right to participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but without a right to vote.
 
• The role includes giving advice to the Government of India upon legal matters and performing other legal duties assigned by the President.
 
• The Attorney General also represents the Government of India in all cases in the Supreme Court in which the Government of India is concerned.
